name: Onigiri
steps: Rinse the rice until the water is nearly clear, then drain well. Put it in a heavy saucepan with the measured cooking water and soak for 30 minutes.

Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid. Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes; the grains should be tender with no loose water.
Fluff the rice and let it cool just until comfortable to handle. Chop the umeboshi finely and divide into 8 portions. Cut the nori into 8 strips.

With clean damp hands, spread a little of the measured salt on your palms. Divide rice into 8 portions. Cup each portion, place umeboshi in the centre, cover with rice and gently compress into a triangle without crushing the grains.
Sprinkle sesame over the rice triangles and wrap each with a nori strip just before eating. Serve promptly; cool and refrigerate any portions being kept for later.
tips: Use sticky Japanese short-grain rice and shape it warm. Umeboshi is salty, so use only a light coating of salt on your hands.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
